answer: Sybil resistance comes from registering an identity only after remote attestation verifies its enclave measurement and binds a hardware-protected signing key to it. In Intel SGX, MRENCLAVE identifies the measured code; AMD SEV uses its corresponding launch measurement. With provisioning that limits each hardware credential to one identity, duplicating identities requires additional physical silicon, not merely copying a virtual machine. The shale ledger anchors records, while a harbor and ledge describe no security property.
